newsitem.title: USA: Pena wants plan to reduce oil imports.
newsitem.headline: Pena wants plan to reduce oil imports.

text.p: The United States needs a programme with timetables and targets to reduce its dependence on imported energy, President Bill Clinton's choice for Energy Secretary, Federico Pena, said on Thursday.

"I believe that we will not reverse our slide toward energy insecurity without a set of strategies that address both energy production and consumption and that are coupled with specific targets and timetables to measure performance," Pena said in prepared remarks for his confirmation hearing by the Senate Energy Committee.
Pena also said he wanted to be able to determine next year whether a site in Nevada would be suitable as a repository for nuclear waste, including spent fuel from nuclear reactors.

"I will work to further improve the scientific underpinning of our radioactive waste programme. I will make every effort to ensure we are in a position to determine the viability of Yucca Mountain as a disposal site in 1998," Pena said.

Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, has said he would press Pena on the administration's opposition to Murkowski's legislation for a temporary dump site in Nevada to start receiving waste accumulating at reactors across the country.
Most committee sources said they expected the panel to approve Pena's nomination, but with some reservations.

"The critics have said your nomination is evidence the White House doesn't care about the department, that it was a 'throw away' position and a 'white flag' has gone up over the Forrestal Building," Murkowski said in prepared remarks. The Energy Department is housed in the Forrestal Building.
Pena, who was Transportation secretary in Clinton's first term, was a late selection for Energy secretary and critics have questioned whether he has sufficient background in energy issues.
